A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CHARTOM-QA research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, tables, prompts, and examples, support reliable comparison despite additions and rearrangements.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLM evaluations, an eight-participant human study on 150 questions, an o1 comparison, and analyses of context length and indirect questions.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds DeepSeek-R1 evaluations, reasoning-trace inspection, and comparisons between automatic metrics and human judgments.

M1.justification: The book-note filtering, extraction/paraphrasing, question verification, distractor construction, and BPC/PR scoring procedures remain unchanged. All ten appendix prompt templates match after accounting for wrapping and renumbering; DeepSeek-R1 is an additional evaluated model.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 1,035 questions from 20 novels, covering four ToM dimensions in English and Chinese through generative and multichoice QA. The added analyses reuse this coverage; the newly stated 150-character count does not establish a dataset expansion.

E2.justification: V2 adds DeepSeek-R1 alongside GPT-4o and o1 in the human-subset comparison in Table 3. Appendix E also actually evaluates ROUGE-L and BERTScore against BPC, whereas v1 only discussed conventional metrics. The six-model main comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include inspecting 100 randomly selected DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces and collecting expert scores from 0 to 1 for generative responses on the human-study subset. Appendix E compares metrics at 2k context with dimension-weighted averages. Existing main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds two focused analyses: human agreement with automatic generative-QA metrics in Appendix E and inspection of DeepSeek-R1 reasoning traces in Section 6.4. It also extends the indirect-question breakdown to DeepSeek-R1. Existing context-length analyses and illustrative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E introduces Pearson-correlation estimation between expert judgments and BPC, ROUGE-L, and BERTScore. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these model comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds DeepSeek-R1 accuracies of 54.0% and 48.7% on all 150 questions at c=0 and c=2k. Section 6.4 reports background/event recall in 76% of inspected traces, and Table 7 adds metric results and human correlations. Table 1 replaces Qwen2's missing English emotion penalty rate at c=2k with 80.1%; other retained main scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains P(a|q,W,G), the plot-window/global-context formulation, and its contextual assumptions. Appendix B retains the same ToM definitions. Neither version presents theoretical proofs, and the new correlation analysis introduces no formal theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the novel-based ToM benchmark, BPC/PR evaluation, and evidence that contextual familiarity benefits humans while current LLMs struggle. Adding DeepSeek-R1 to the abstract and conclusion extends supporting evidence without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets DeepSeek-R1 traces as supporting contextual reasoning and emotions as less dependent on global context. It adds arguments about character diversity mitigating bias and BPC's agreement with humans. The specific suggestion that o1 mainly exploits superficial clues becomes a broader contextual-understanding limitation; the limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promise to release data after review with GitHub and Hugging Face dataset download locations. It also discloses 150 unique target characters and additional human-study data-handling information. Existing construction and evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of benchmarks such as FANTOM, OpenToM, and COKE. New Appendix C and Table 5 systematically compare eleven prior benchmarks by task, construction, and character background, substantially developing the novelty argument. References also add DeepSeek-R1 and remove Jiang and Ferraro (2024) and v1's Zhou et al. (2023b).

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, revises several headings, and expands related-work and appendix explanations. New Appendices C and E shift later labels, but the main narrative sequence and most methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds a front-page illustration of the existing Father Goriot case and new Tables 5 and 7, resizes and rearranges construction figures, and expands Table 3. Several appendix prompt tables change from single-column boxes to full-width displays, producing substantial layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 adds initial empirical support for BPC through human correlations of 0.92 versus 0.72 for ROUGE-L and 0.81 for BERTScore, extends comparison to DeepSeek-R1, and supplies dataset download locations. These improve evidential support and usability. The gain remains limited because Appendix E sparsely documents rating and correlation procedures and provides no corresponding human validation of PR.
